skill.name: deployment-engineer
skill.description: Designs secure CI/CD pipelines, GitOps workflows, progressive delivery strategies, deployment controls, rollback plans, and observability for modern application platforms.
skill.summary: Plan secure, observable deployment workflows with quality gates, progressive delivery, and reliable rollback procedures.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The single static finding is a false positive because the cited line advises against unsafe production rollouts. No prompt injection, malicious intent, or other semantic security issue was found.

static_findings.snippet: - Avoid production rollouts without approvals and rollback plans.

finding_verdicts.reason: The cited line warns users to avoid production rollouts without approvals and rollback plans. It contains no system reconnaissance instruction or request to collect host information.

content.value_statement: Complex releases fail when pipelines lack clear controls, validation, observability, and rollback procedures. This skill designs practical CI/CD and GitOps workflows for reliable delivery.
actual_capabilities: Designs CI/CD stages with tests, security scans, approvals, and release gates.
Recommends GitOps repository structures, promotion flows, and configuration management patterns.
Plans rolling, blue-green, canary, and zero-downtime deployment strategies.
Defines health checks, observability signals, rollback triggers, and incident procedures.
Advises on container hardening, image scanning, signing, and supply chain controls.
Creates deployment runbooks for multiple environments, Kubernetes platforms, and infrastructure workflows.
limitations: Cannot inspect live infrastructure, permissions, secrets, or deployment state without supplied evidence.
Does not replace staging validation, security review, change approval, or platform owner sign-off.
Recommendations require adaptation to the selected cloud, CI/CD platform, and organizational controls.
Cannot guarantee zero downtime or rollback success without application-specific testing.

use_cases.title: Standardize Release Pipelines
use_cases.description: Create reusable stages, quality gates, approvals, and promotion rules across application teams.

use_cases.title: Plan Progressive Delivery
use_cases.description: Define canary increments, health metrics, rollback thresholds, and operator decision points.

use_cases.title: Secure Container Releases
use_cases.description: Add image scanning, signing, provenance, secret controls, and policy enforcement to delivery workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Deployment Process
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this deployment process: [process]. Identify missing tests, approvals, monitoring, and rollback steps. Recommend a safer sequence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of an existing release process

prompt_templates.title: Design a CI/CD Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a CI/CD pipeline for [application] on [platform]. Include stages, gates, artifact handling, environment promotion, secrets, and rollback.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Canary Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a canary deployment for [service]. Define traffic increments, success metrics, observation periods, stop conditions, rollback triggers, and approvals.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Enterprise GitOps Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a GitOps operating model for [organization]. Cover repositories, tenancy, policy, secrets, promotion, drift, disaster recovery, and audit evidence.

output_examples.input: Design a release pipeline for a containerized API with staging and production environments.
output: Build one signed image, generate an SBOM, and scan the image before publishing.
Deploy the immutable image to staging, then run integration, security, and smoke tests.
Require production approval before a canary rollout with health-based rollback.

output_examples.input: Recommend rollback criteria for a canary deployment.
output_examples.output: Rollback when error rate, latency, saturation, or business failures exceed agreed thresholds during the observation window.

output_examples.input: Outline a secure GitOps promotion workflow.
output: Promote reviewed version references through environment branches or directories.
Use policy checks and required approvals before merging production changes.
Reconcile signed artifacts while monitoring drift and deployment health.

best_practices: Provide the application architecture, target environments, compliance needs, and current release process.
Define measurable success, failure, and rollback thresholds before selecting a deployment strategy.
Validate recommendations in staging and preserve human approval for sensitive production changes.
anti_patterns: Do not provide production secrets, private keys, tokens, or unredacted credentials.
Do not apply generic pipeline advice without checking platform constraints and application behavior.
Do not remove approvals or rollback controls solely to increase deployment speed.

faq.question: Which deployment platforms does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers major CI/CD services, GitOps tools, container platforms, Kubernetes, and common cloud deployment services.

faq.question: Can it deploy directly to my environment?
faq.answer: The skill provides plans and implementation guidance. Actual execution depends on available tools, permissions, and explicit user approval.

faq.question: Does it support Kubernetes deployments?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers rollout strategies, Helm, Kustomize, GitOps controllers, health checks, policies, and resource management.

faq.question: Can it help with security and compliance?
faq.answer: Yes. It can recommend scanning, signing, provenance, secret management, policy gates, and audit evidence.

faq.question: What information produces the best result?
faq.answer: Provide architecture, deployment targets, current tooling, environments, risk tolerance, compliance requirements, and rollback constraints.

faq.question: Does it guarantee zero-downtime deployments?
faq.answer: No. Zero downtime requires compatible application behavior, infrastructure capacity, tested migrations, health signals, and validated rollback procedures.
